newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed Tuesday, with prices seen consolidating near current levels, traders said.
CSCE was closed Monday in observance of U.S. Memorial Day.

Friday, New York arabica futures ended mostly lower, pressured by speculative profit taking. July settled down 3.45 cents at 256.85 cents a lb after ranging from 262.25 to 255.50. Second-position September closed 3.90 cents lower at 226.05 cents, while the back months finished down 3.65 to up 0.50.
Technically, July support was seen at 250.00 cents. On the upside, traders pegged resistance at 262.00 cents, followed by July's life-of-contract high set Thursday of 265.00 cents.
There was no damaging cold in Brazil's coffee belt over the weekend and no freeze was forecast for the rest of this week, Weather Services Corp said in its daily update.

The latest CFTC Commitments of Traders report for the two weeks ended May 20 showed non-comercial long positions increased by 983 lots, to 8,519 lots. Non-commercial short positions increased by 784 lots, to 1,762 lots.
Commercial long positions rose by 87 lots in the two weeks, to 7,750 lots, while commercial short positions rose by 881 lots, to 18,846 lots.
Nonreportable long positions fell by 522 lots, to 12,504 lots and nonreportable short positions fell by 1,117 lots, to 8,165 lots.
After Friday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were unchanged, at 49,712 60-kg bags as of May 22. There was no coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
London July robusta futures were lower in quiet dealings early Tuesday, pressured by origin and trade selling. LIFFE July fell $13 at the midday break, to $2,073, after ranging from $1,84 to $2,065.
The London market was also closed on Monday for a holiday.
